picks.title: What does it mean to have a personal relationship with Jesus?
picks.summary: Fr. James Martin, S.J., welcomes Susan Stabile, a spiritual director and retreat leader in the Ignatian tradition onto “The Spiritual Life” podcast. Susan was raised Catholic, but spent twenty years practicing Buddhism (and was ordained a Tibetan Buddhist nun) before returning to Catholicism. She now serves as Distinguished Senior Fellow at the University of St. Thomas, as well as adjunct instructor in Theology at St. Catherine’s University, where she is also Co-Director of a Contemplative Practices initiative. picks.showTitle: Sunday Homilies with Fr. Mike Schmitz
picks.title: 09/20/26 Blind Spots: Entitlement
picks.summary: Homily from the Twenty-fifth Sunday in Ordinary Time. God does not owe me anything. Entitlement does not always look like entitlement. Sometimes, it simply feels like getting what we deserve. Whether it comes from pride or pain, we can believe that we are owed more. But grace is, by definition, an undeserved gift. The cure for entitlement is to stop asking what we are owed and to start asking what God has entrusted to us...and then receive it with gratitude. Mass Readings from September 20, 2026: Isaiah 55:6-9 Psalm 145:2-3, 8-9, 17-18Philippians 1:20c-24, 27a Matthew 20:1-16a]]>
picks.reason: Homily on entitlement and grace from a Catholic priest, rooted in Scripture and Catholic teaching.

picks.showTitle: The Fr. Mike Schmitz Catholic Podcast
picks.title: The Power of Adoration
picks.summary:
Fr. Mike Schmitz shares the words of Jesus that have changed his life:

“Could you not watch with me one hour?”

These words have deeply shaped Fr. Mike’s life as well as the life of Blessed Fulton Sheen, who made a daily holy hour. 

Whether it’s a full hour or just five quiet minutes, spending time with Jesus in the Eucharist can transform your life.

Discover the power of simply being with Jesus and see how Eucharistic prayer has changed the lives of Fr. Mike Schmitz and Fulton Sheen.]]>
picks.reason: Exploration of Eucharistic adoration's transformative power in Catholic spiritual life.

picks.showTitle: The Rosary in a Year (with Fr. Mark-Mary Ames)
picks.title: Day 270: The Luminous and Sorrowful Mysteries
picks.summary:
Concluding the Luminous mysteries, we recall Our Lord’s divinity as he is transfigured on the mountain and shares himself, body, blood, soul, and divinity with us in the Eucharist. Stepping into the Sorrowful mysteries, after the Last Supper we have just mediated upon, we witness his agony in preparation to offer himself up for our salvation. Today’s focus is the mysteries of the Transfiguration, the Institution of the Eucharist, and the Agony in the Garden. We will be praying three decades of the Rosary.

For the complete prayer plan, visit https://ascensionpress.com/riy. ]]>
picks.reason: Meditation on the Luminous and Sorrowful Mysteries of the Rosary, central Catholic devotion.
